original_value: Many Internet of Things (IoT) applications are emerging and evolving rapidly thanks to widespread open-source hardware platforms. Most of the high-end open-source IoT platforms include built-in peripherals, such as the universal asynchronous receiver and transmitter (UART), pulse width modulation (PWM), general purpose input output (GPIO) ports and timers, and have enough computation power to run embedded operating systems such as Linux. However, each IoT platform has its own way of configuring peripherals, and it is difficult for programmers or users to configure the same peripheral on a different platform. Although diverse open-source IoT platforms are widespread, the difficulty in programming those platforms hinders the growth of IoT applications. Therefore, we propose an easy and convenient way to program and configure the operation of each peripheral using a user-friendly Web-based software framework. Through the implementation of the software framework and the real mobile robot application development along with it, we show the feasibility of the proposed software framework, named SoEasy.

result.paraphrase: The rapid growth of many Internet of Things (IoT) applications is being driven by the broad availability of open-source hardware platforms. Most high-end open-source IoT platforms come with built-in peripherals such as UART, PWM, GPIO ports, and timers, and they have sufficient computing power to run embedded operating systems like Linux. However, each platform uses its own method for configuring peripherals, making it hard for programmers or users to set up the same peripheral on another platform. Although open-source IoT platforms are widely used, the difficulty of programming them slows the expansion of IoT applications. To address this, we propose a user-friendly Web-based software framework that provides an easy and convenient way to program and configure each peripheral. By implementing the framework and developing a real mobile robot application with it, we demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed software framework, called SoEasy.
